title: What side projects have you enjoyed the most?
content_html:
I enjoy traditional roguelikes, and my favorite is Sil-Q: https://github.com/sil-quirk/sil-q

For those who are new to Sil / Sil-Q, it is a roguelike forked from Angband that focuses on:

  • fidelity to Tolkien
  • tactical gameplay, with sophisticated combat and stealth systems
  • a shorter, more intense experience

It does not have classes. Characters are built up as the player chooses synergising skills. Both seeing and killing enemies gets you experience, but diminishing returns from repeated encounters with the same enemies make grinding an unhelpful strategy.

I‘d describe it as a dungeon heist game set in the First Age of Middle-earth. Others called it "Angband: Black Ops" because it has a very streamlined gameplay, with runs lasting 30-60mins, which is more compatible with other day to day commitments than games like NetHack or Angband.

This year I decided to contribute back and wake the dormant project from its slumber. Quirk, the original dev who worked on this Angband variant for 10 years, hasn‘t much time available today. I collaborated with him and MicroChasm, the game‘s tileset artist, to modernize the codebase, fix all known bugs of the past three years, generate ready-to-use downloads for Win/Mac/Linux, and add a few gameplay features and UX improvements. I‘m also working on an updated official manual (PDF and online) along with a proper website.

I have enjoyed working on my first C project, though understanding Sil-Q‘s four different DIY graphic stacks (Win / Mac / Linux + console) has been…quite the experience. Some of its code dates back almost 40 years, for platforms like Amiga, NeXT, SGI, Dec ALPHA, and RISC OS—most of which was untested, essentially rotten code by now. Like entering the mines of Moria and straying from the trodden path. (Almost all of which I cleaned up through tedious work resulting in a humongous PR. That was a bit scary. The codebase had 0 tests, now it has at least a few.)

All gory details here: https://github.com/sil-quirk/sil-q/releases/tag/v1.5.1-beta1

It‘s been wonderful to contribute to a free, open source game that has such a long lineage and pedigree (its code traces back to the original Rogue, which coined the genre), and even more to collaborate with individuals like Quirk, MicroChasm, and backwardsEric (the lead dev of Angband) to bring a little bit of joy to the world. Even if Sil-Q is a niche game in a niche genre for a tiny playerbase. Still, the new beta has 900 downloads by now.

Personally, it has been a soothing feeling to work on such a long-lasting project while the rest of our profession seems to explode with vibe-coded slop projects, many of which are or will be abandoned soon after their creation.

If you happen to play the game: enjoy, glhf!

content_html_zh:
我喜欢传统的 Roguelike 游戏，最喜欢的是 Sil-Q：https://github.com/sil-quirk/sil-q

对于那些刚接触 Sil / Sil-Q 的人来说，这是一款从 Angband 衍生出来的 Roguelike 游戏，其重点是： 忠实于托尔金的战术游戏玩法，具有复杂的战斗和潜行系统 更短、更激烈的体验 它没有类别。 当玩家选择协同技能时，角色就会建立起来。 看到和杀死敌人都能让你获得经验，但重复遭遇相同敌人所带来的收益递减使得磨练成为一种无益的策略。

我将其描述为一款以中土第一纪元为背景的地下城抢劫游戏。 其他人将其称为“Angband：黑色行动”，因为它具有非常精简的游戏玩法，运行时间持续 30-60 分钟，这比 NetHack 或 Angband 等游戏更适合其他日常任务。

今年我决定回馈社会，将这个沉睡的项目从沉睡中唤醒。 Quirk 是最初的开发者，他在这个 Angband 变体上工作了 10 年，现在没有太多时间。 我与他和游戏的图块艺术家 MicroChasm 合作，对代码库进行了现代化改造，修复了过去三年中所有已知的错误，为 Win/Mac/Linux 生成了即用型下载，并添加了一些游戏功能和用户体验改进。 我还在制作更新的官方手册（PDF 和在线）以及适当的网站。

我很享受我的第一个 C 项目的工作，尽管了解 Sil-Q 的四种不同的 DIY 图形堆栈（Win / Mac / Linux + 控制台）已经……相当不错的体验。 它的一些代码可以追溯到近 40 年前，适用于 Amiga、NeXT、SGI、Dec ALPHA 和 RISC OS 等平台，其中大部分尚未经过测试，到目前为止基本上都是烂代码。 就像进入莫瑞亚的矿井并偏离了常走的道路一样。 （几乎所有这些都是我通过繁琐的工作清理干净的，从而产生了巨大的公关。 那就有点吓人了。 代码库有 0 次测试，现在至少有一些。）

所有血淋淋的细节都在这里：https://github.com/sil-quirk/sil-q/releases/tag/v1.5.1-beta1

能够为一款拥有如此悠久的血统和血统的免费开源游戏做出贡献（其代码可以追溯到创造了该类型的原始 Rogue），并且与 Quirk、MicroChasm 和backwardsEric（Angband 的首席开发人员）等个人合作，为世界带来一点欢乐，这真是太棒了。 即使《Sil-Q》是一款适合小众玩家的小众游戏。 尽管如此，新测试版目前仍有 900 次下载。

就我个人而言，在这样一个持久的项目上工作是一种令人舒缓的感觉，而我们职业的其他部分似乎因振动编码的垃圾项目而爆炸，其中许多项目在创建后不久就被放弃或将被放弃。

如果你碰巧玩这个游戏：享受吧，glhf！
